en.html:
We joined the Ootori pair and began the journey home.
Rain, absent when I left, now filled the space between earth and sky. I had to borrow an umbrella from Hachimangu.

Nagakura's preparedness knew no restraint. From somewhere she produced umbrellas, and the two women, old and young, sheltered beneath their own.
Kanae's was plain white.

Perhaps she liked it. She played with it, turning it round and round in her hand.
She seemed in good spirits.

We joined the Ootori pair and began the journey home.
Rain, absent when I left, now filled the space between earth and sky. I had to borrow an umbrella from Hachimangu.

Nagakura's preparedness knew no restraint. From somewhere she produced umbrellas, and the two women, old and young, sheltered beneath their own.
Kanae's was plain white.

Perhaps she liked it. She played with it, turning it round and round in her hand.
She seemed in good spirits.

大鳥主従と合流し、帰路につく。
　出がけには無かった雨が天地の狭間を満たしており、
俺は八幡宮で傘を借りねばならなかった。

　野放図なまでに用意のいい永倉侍従が何処からとも
なく取り出したので、老若の女性二人組は自前の傘を
差している。
　香奈枝嬢のそれは、白の無地。

　気に入りなのか、手の中で弄んでくるくると回して
いる。
　機嫌が良さそうだった。

en.html:
Kanae"Nanny, are you allowing a fixed idea to govern you? Nobody has decreed that rain must be unpleasant."
Sayo"Quite so. A blessing, they also call the rain."
Kanae"Exactly. ...Ufufufufufufufufu."
Sayo"W-what has happened, Miss!? That laugh—so devilish, so suspicious, so entirely outside the human species! This Sayo very nearly threw a stone!"
Kanae"Ufu... agriculture has no exclusive right to the blessings of rain—"
Kanae"Romance between men and women may receive them also!"

Sayo"Oh... a fearsome strategy indeed! The whole sky has been sent out to argue your case. Naturally, this Sayo's mistress cannot be an ordinary thinker."
Kanae"Uffufufu..."
Sayo"You have arranged an advantage, Miss, not an invitation. Do this deliberately, and you are not improving the weather for the gentleman. You are joining it."
Kanae"That risk is precisely why courage is required! If I wait to be welcomed before I dare, where is the bravery? You are proving my point, Nanny. To gain the fruit of love, one needs courage enough to be called reckless!"
Kanae"Tell me, Kageaki—you agree, surely?"
Kageaki"Yes."
Kanae"Then all this courage of mine... you will accept it?"
Kageaki"Yes."
Kanae"Ah, Nanny, did you hear? At last my feelings have reached him...!"
Sayo"Congratulations, Miss! Two yeses, and a complete understanding. Though he has not heard one word of what you said."

en.html:
The conversation went in one ear and out of the other.
My mind was occupied already.

What I had learned of the Prince's and the Chief's true intentions.
—They had no intention of judging Kageaki Minato.

The evil I had committed would be let pass. No examination under the law, no punishment to match it.

If these third parties, who knew everything, did not intend to act, then that was necessarily what would happen.

...Absurd.

Such—such an absurd thing.
Could it be permitted?

It could not...

　――彼らは湊斗景明を裁くつもりがない。

必然、そうなる。

　許されて良いのか。

　良い筈はない……。

en.html:
Kageaki"..."
Kanae"...Now I think of it, you do seem a little low, Kageaki. Whatever is the matter?"
Sayo"Do you think so? That gloomy face, that air of depression capable of lowering share prices by proximity... our usual Minato, surely."
Kanae"But ordinarily, after so much making a move from me, would he not cry, 'Enough talking round it! You want my attention, don't you? Then here I am!' and come charging over?"
Sayo"Put it like that, and I can almost see it."
Kanae"Perhaps something happened at Hachimangu."
Sayo"Something?"
Kanae"Something that would bring a gentleman so low..."
Sayo"Yes?"
Kanae"...Has he become sensible?"
Sayo"One moment."
Kanae"Entirely, incurably reasonable...?"
Sayo"I said, one moment, Miss."
Kanae"At his age, too... Sayo, what shall I do? I want to tell him, 'Even with common sense, I still like you!' But perhaps that would only wound him?"
Sayo"How, precisely, would this common sense have been discovered at Hachimangu?"
Kanae"................................"
Kanae"Oh..."
Sayo"As a human being, you are beyond assistance now, Miss."
Kageaki"..."

en.html:
Having brought the conversation to a rather rapid conclusion, Kanae promptly entered the lane.
There was no time to call her back.

I watched the white umbrella go, then let out a breath.
To be honest, part of me was relieved.

Everything was an effort now.
The climb to Zeniarai Benten was not even a few dozen meters in elevation. Even so, it was more than I could manage just then.

Far easier to stand in the rain and wait for her return. Preferable, even.
I need think nothing. Consider nothing.

Nagakura stood silently, scarcely making her presence felt. Perhaps she had read my mood and was being considerate.
That troubled me in its own way—but I did not want to think even about that.

...Still, why had Captain Ootori left her attendant?
Surely she could have taken her along.

Come to think of it, just before heading for Genjiyama, the two had seemed to exchange a silent glance. That was—

...Enough.

Thinking was terribly tiring now...

ja.html:
やや早口に会話をまとめると、香奈枝嬢はさっさと
路地へ入っていってしまった。
　呼び止める間もない。

　白い傘を見送って、ふと息をつく。
　正直、安堵する部分もあった。

　今は何をするのも億劫だ。
　銭洗弁天までは標高にして何十メートルもないが、
それでも今の自分には荷が重い。

　彼女の帰りを雨の下に立ち尽くして待つ方がずっと
楽だった。むしろそれなら望むところだった。
　何も思わず、何も考えずにいられる。

　永倉侍従は黙して佇立し、ろくに気配さえ感じさせ
ない。こちらの心境を読み、気を遣ったのかもしれな
かった。それはそれで心苦しかったが――今はそんな
ことも考えたくはない。

　……しかし、なぜ大鳥大尉は侍従を残したのだろう。
　一緒に連れて行けば良さそうなものだが。

　そういえば源氏山へ向かう間際、二人で無言の視線
を交し合ったように見えたが――あれは――
　
　……やめよう。

　物を考えると、今は酷く疲れる……。

Sayo"Has something happened, Miss?"
Kanae"...No. Nothing very much."
Kanae"Only, I heard a rather unpleasant story..."
Sayo"At Benten?"
Kanae"Yes. The chief priest happened to be there, so I asked about the shrine's history. And—"
Sayo"He informed you that the shrine actually honors an octopus-like god, asleep in a city on the seabed?"
Kanae"That would be deeply unpleasant, but no. ...It was such an interesting shrine, with a cave for its entrance. I remarked that it must be a fine place for children to play."
Kanae"His face darkened. Until recently, he said, a lively group of four had often visited. But not any longer..."
Sayo"What...?"
Kanae"...Misfortune befell all four. One disappeared in a nearby bamboo grove and has not been seen since."

Kanae"Why is it not the other way round?"
Sayo"Why is it not, indeed?"
Kanae"Kageaki."
Kanae"Why?"

en.html:
Why.
Why.

Why was I alone still alive?
Killing and killing and killing and killing, I had driven so many into a world without rain. Why was I alone permitted still to walk beneath it?

Wrong.
Unreasonable.
Unjust.

It could not be permitted.
I must be punished.

—Yet forgiveness was being prepared for me.

Those who knew my crimes would not denounce them. They forgave... praised them as achievements, even... spoke of giving me rest.

Why.

Why————was such injustice allowed to pass!

　どうして――そんな理不尽が通る！
